subject: SpectraHealth SLA & escalation packaging — updated pricing proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@spectrahealth.com>
Cc: infra-team@spectrahealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA proposal for SpectraHealth (uptime tiers & escalation coverage)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. As discussed, I’m attaching a baseline proposal that maps the SLA tiers you outlined to our packaging options. Highlights:

- Three uptime bands: 99.5%, 99.9%, 99.95% (with incremental credits)
- Response lanes: Standard (8x5 <24hr), Priority (24x7 <4hr), Critical (SRE escalation <1hr)
- Escalation coverage: direct SRE pager for Critical + named AM for Priority
- Optional on-call retainer for guaranteed 1-hour triage during Major Incidents

I attached redwood_quote_v3.xlsx with line-item pricing and a separate PDF you shared for reference (spectra_sla_requirements.pdf). We priced the Priority lane as an add-on per seat and included a notional 10% volume discount for a 12-month commit.

Questions for you:
1) Are the three uptime bands aligned with your procurement rubric?
2) Do you anticipate using the Critical escalation lane more than 2x/yr (affects retainer sizing)?
3) Any compliance items to fold into the SOW for Private deployment?

If that looks reasonable I can turn it into a DocuSign-ready SOW and a clean pricing worksheet.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales (West)
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Attachments: redwood_quote_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), spectra_sla_requirements.pdf (pdf)
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@spectrahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial SLA proposal for SpectraHealth (uptime tiers & escalation coverage)

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from procurement / infra below: 

- Uptime bands: We prefer 99.9 as our target (customer-facing) with 99.95 for peak services (patient-critical). 99.5 is acceptable for analytics/backfill workloads.
- Response times: Critical <1hr is a hard ask, but procurement will push on the retainer fee if we have to pay for an always-on SRE.
- Escalation: We require a named escalation roster and a quarterly runbook review tied to the SOW.

Procurement asked whether you can provide a 15% discount off list for a 24-month commitment and whether the retainer can be structured as a quarterly fee rather than upfront. Also: can you confirm that incident credits are pro-rated monthly?

I’ve attached the internal SLA checklist (spectra_sla_requirements.pdf) — most of our items are already reflected, but there are a couple of compliance evidence asks for SOC2 handling of KV cache logs.

Cc’ing procurement now (procurement@spectrahealth.com).

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform Operations
SpectraHealth
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SpectraHealth SLA & escalation packaging — pricing ask (internal)

Kim, Connor — forwarding Spectra’s response. They asked for a 15% discount on list for a 24-month commitment and a quarterly retainer payment option for the on-call. They also pressed on pro-rated incident credits and want SOC2 KV cache handling language in the SOW.

Quick asks:
- Is 15% feasible if we require a 12-month minimum committed spend and annual true-up? They sign faster if 24 months.
- Can we structure the retainer as a quarterly charge (we’d prefer monthly or annual w/ amortization).
- Any redlines on the SOC2 evidence for KV cache logs — Connor / SRE implications?

FYI I’m trying to avoid opening a custom SLA negotiation if we can fit them into an established Premium Support pack. I’ve attached redwood_quote_v3.xlsx for annotation.

—Jordan
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 10:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SpectraHealth SLA & escalation packaging — pricing ask (internal)

Jordan / Connor — reviewed. My recommendations below and I attached an annotated worksheet (redwood_quote_v3_annotated.xlsx):

1) Discounting: We can offer 15% but only if both conditions are met: (a) 24-month term AND (b) commit to a minimum $275k ARR equivalent (we should tie to monthly token consumption bands). Otherwise cap at 12% for 18-months or 10% for 12-months.

2) Retainer payment cadence: Accept quarterly billing for the retainer, but structure it as a quarterly pre-pay that is refundable/adjustable after the first 90 days based on incident consumption. That preserves cashflow visibility for them and reduces our risk.

3) Incident credits: Yes, pro-rated monthly. Document the cap (max credits per quarter = 5% of spend) and tie crediting logic to the published incident SLA matrix — this avoids open-ended exposure.

4) SOC2 / KV cache logs: Connor — we need to confirm retention windows and redaction. If Spectra wants full KV-level retention for 90 days we must pull in SRE and security. Suggest we offer a SOC2 attestation + hardened audit logs export (not raw KV dumps) as part of Private deployment SOW; for hosted we can offer an encrypted audit trail and retention configurable up to 90 days with an additional fee.

5) Packaging suggestion: Put Spectra onto Priority lane for patient-critical services (99.95) and run analytics on Hosted with 99.5. That maps to a blended price and simplifies operations.

If you want I’ll draft the concession language and updated pricing cells. We should also include an exec summary clause that gives a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to 5% of first-quarter retainer) if they sign within 21 days.

—Kimberly
Head of GTM Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@spectrahealth.com>, procurement@spectrahealth.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final: SLA packaging + pricing (24-month concession & quarterly retainer option)

Elena / procurement team —

Thanks for the clarity. Per our internal review we’ve updated the quote and packaging to reflect your asks. Summary of changes from the worksheet attached earlier: 

- 24-month commitment: we can offer 15% off list conditioned on a minimum $275k ARR-equivalent commitment (detailed in pricing cells).
- Retainer: quarterly pre-pay accepted, refundable/adjustable after 90 days based on consumption; onboarding credit equal to 5% of first-quarter retainer if signed within 21 days.
- Incident credits: pro-rated monthly; quarterly cap at 5% of spend; crediting algorithm documented in the SOW Appendix B.
- SOC2 / KV cache handling: For Private deployments we’ll include hardened audit logs export and SOC2 attestation language. For hosted we can enable audit log retention up to 90 days (additional fee) and provide redacted KV traces for post-incident review.

I attached an updated pricing worksheet (redwood_quote_v3.xlsx — now version 3.1) and a short SOW addendum draft. If this aligns, I’ll convert to DocuSign. For convenience here is the signing link: https://www.docusign.com/SH-SLA-042-sign

Next steps I propose:
- Procurement confirms minimum spend threshold OK (Elena) — by EOD Thursday
- I create DocuSign SOW + PO instructions and loop legal if any contract redlines appear
- Onboarding kickoff scheduled within 10 business days of signature

Open to a quick call if you want to walk pricing cells.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales (West)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_quote_v3.xlsx (pricing worksheet v3.1), SOW_addendum_draft.docx (text)
